name: Oklahoma
standard: WCAG 2.1 AA minimum (or the current DOJ standard), plus Section 508; OMES 'Accessibility of Information and Communication Technology Standard' (effective 2025-06-27)

laws.summary: Requires state agencies to make IT accessible to people with disabilities unless an undue burden applies, and directs OMES to set accessibility standards.
Administrative rules for IT accessibility, including the complaint process and remediation recordkeeping.

laws.cite: 28 CFR Part 35, Subpart H (ADA Title II web/mobile rule, 2024; compliance dates extended by DOJ IFR effective 2026-04-20)
laws.summary: Requires state and local government web content and mobile apps to conform to WCAG 2.1 AA, with compliance dates now 2027-04-26 (population 50,000+) and 2028-04-26 (smaller entities and special districts).

policy_docs.title: Accessibility of Information and Communication Technology Standard (OMES IS, effective 06/27/2025)

applies_to: State agencies in the executive and judicial branches, including the State Regents for Higher Education and CareerTech; excludes political subdivisions (ADA Title II floor still applies to them). Covers websites, web apps, public documents, software, and paid or free third-party products.

deadlines.what: ADA Title II floor: state government and local entities with population 50,000+ must conform to WCAG 2.1 AA (extended from 2026-04-24 by the 2026 DOJ IFR).
ADA Title II floor: local entities under 50,000 population and special district governments (extended from 2027-04-26).

requires: Mandatory accessibility contract clause in every ICT acquisition
VPAT/ACR from supplier at contract execution (off-the-shelf) or on delivery (custom); the conformance claim is a material contract term
Verify ICT acquisitions by testing (automated, manual, expert, third-party, or user testing)
Remediate noncompliant ICT within a reasonable time and keep records of issues and remediation
mobile: implied — covers websites, web-based applications and digital platforms and adopts the DOJ Title II rule, but does not name mobile apps.
procurement: Mandatory WCAG 2.1 AA contract clause; completed VPAT required; accessibility checks built into agency procurement.
enforcement: Any individual may file a complaint under OAC 260:15-1-1 et seq.; employees violating the standard face discipline.
notes: The standard itself was opened and read. The statute and OAC chapter links come from search results and were not opened.
